pairs.why: A's open-sided box with chunky seeds and flat plank roof reads closer to the real feeder than B's arched, smaller house form.
A matches the real ball's tilted view with the cap toward the top-front and its broad glossy panels, while B is a flatter front-on view.
B's fruit sits inside a clearer, more visible glass plate like the real card, while A's fruit spills over a thin plate edge.
A is built like the real calculator with labeled keys and cyan operator buttons, while B has blank keys and reads as a generic toy.
A's simpler cylindrical stools and chunky pedestal are a bit nearer the real card's plain stone build than B's more ornate moulded pedestal.
B has the real card's fine small dot texture and proportions, while A's oversized bumps look toy-like.
A's smoother candy-gloss dome with cyan inner glow is closer to the real jellyfish's finish than B's busier, bubble-flecked rendering.
A has the smoother, cleaner skin of the real cards, while B adds speckled surface texture that the lessons mark as too texture-y.
